title: The walking shadow
offscreen: It works indoors too: a bottle of water on a sunny windowsill, and its shadow marked on the floor with a piece of masking tape.

materials.label: A stone or a piece of chalk to mark with
Something outdoors that doesn't move: a post, a tree, a big flowerpot

steps.text: With a grown-up, choose something outdoors that always stays put, and a time of day.
Put the stone right on the tip of its shadow.
In the notebook draw the object and the shadow, and write the time.
Come back on the next days at the same time: is the shadow longer or shorter? Nearer or further than the stone?

levels.control: Yesterday's stone: today's shadow is compared with it, no measuring needed.
levels.observe: Whether they make a prediction for the next day on their own, and what words they use to compare.

intro.bo: {nome}, today we look outside, not here. Call a grown-up: you need a stone and a spot.
intro.pilu: {nome}, shadows change slowly. You only find out by coming back to look, day after day.
intro.tango: {nome}! A walking shadow! I'll stay here on guard. You go outside with a grown-up.

outro.bo: The stone stays there, {nome}. Tomorrow you go back at the same time.
outro.pilu: The time is written in your notebook, {nome}: tomorrow you'll need it to compare.
outro.tango: Done! {nome}, will you tell me tomorrow if the shadow has moved?
